description: IFASTAT is the statistics service of the International Fertilizer Association, covering the supply, demand and trade of fertilizers and their raw materials and intermediates. Its indicators are capacity, production, imports, exports, home deliveries, apparent consumption for all uses, and fertilizer consumption for plant nutrition, by product and nutrient; it does not publish prices. It is produced by the International Fertilizer Association (IFA), the global industry association. Coverage is global by country and region, with supply and trade data from 2000 and consumption data from 1961; data are annual, with quarterly and half-yearly figures for some indicators, released with a nine-month lag for antitrust reasons. Access is through an online data query, visualisations and reports: regional summaries and national consumption data are open to non-members, while country-level supply and trade data are reserved for members under a data licence agreement. Caveats: coverage varies by indicator and product with market concentration, and members may not redistribute the data. For simulation it maps where fertilizer is produced and traded, the basis for modelling how gas supply cuts or blocked chokepoints such as the Strait of Hormuz, which IFA highlights, would spread to farm output. It is related to the global crop-specific nitrogen fertilization record in this catalogue, which builds on IFASTAT consumption data.
